explanation: Dysgerminoma is the most common malignant germ cell tumor in young females (equivalent to male seminoma). Histology shows clear 'fried egg' cells with lymphocytic stroma. Tumor markers include elevated LDH and hCG.

question: [High-Yield Clinical Concept #993]: Which enzyme deficiency in the hexose monophosphate (HMP) shunt results in episodic intravascular hemolysis, Heinz bodies, and bite cells following oxidative stress (e.g., fava beans, primaquine, infection)?
explanation: G6PD deficiency is an X-linked recessive disorder impairing NADPH generation in the HMP shunt. Without NADPH, glutathione cannot be reduced, leaving erythrocytes vulnerable to oxidative stress. question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-2]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #3): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-4]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #5): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_c: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_d: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_e: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-6]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #7): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_c: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-8]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-174]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #175): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_a: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-176]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #177): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-178]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #179): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-180]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #181): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_b: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_c: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_d: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_e: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-314]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #315): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-316]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #317): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_c: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_d: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_e: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-318]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #319): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_e: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-320]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-406]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #407): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_d: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-408]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #409): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-410]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #411): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-412]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #413): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_b: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis

option_d: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_e: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-546]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #547): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-548]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #549): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_b: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_c: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_d: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_e: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-550]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #551): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_c: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-552]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-638]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #639): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_b: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-640]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #641): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-642]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #643): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-644]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #645): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_b: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_c: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_d: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_e: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-824]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #825): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-826]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #827): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-828]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #829): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_c: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_d: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_e: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-830]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1148]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1149): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_c: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_d: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_e: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1150]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1151): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_a: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1152]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1153): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1154]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1155): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1194]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1195): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1196]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1197): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_c: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_d: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_e: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1198]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1199): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_b: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1200]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1201): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1564]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1565): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_b: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_c: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_d: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_e: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1566]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1567): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_e: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1568]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1569): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.

question: A 19-year-old male athlete experiences sudden-onset lightheadedness and palpitations while running. Resting 12-lead ECG demonstrates a short PR interval (<120 ms), a slurred upstroke of the QRS complex (delta wave), and QRS widening. The patient is diagnosed with ventricular pre-excitation. What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1570]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1571): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

What is the name of the accessory electrical conduction pathway bypassing the AV node in this condition? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1610]
explanation: Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome is caused by an accessory pathway (Bundle of Kent) that directly connects the atria to the ventricles, bypassing the normal AV nodal delay. This results in ventricular pre-excitation characterized by a short PR interval, delta wave, and widened QRS complex.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1611): Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A (MEN 2A) and type 2B (MEN 2B) are both caused by gain-of-function proto-oncogene mutations in which gene?
explanation: MEN 2A (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, parathyroid hyperplasia) and MEN 2B (medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, marfanoid habitus) are autosomal dominant syndromes caused by germline gain-of-function mutations in the RET proto-oncogene (receptor tyrosine kinase).

question: A 45-year-old woman presents with difficulty swallowing solid foods, fatigue, and weakness. Physical examination reveals spoon-shaped fingernails (koilonychia), mucosal pallor, and angular cheilitis. Barium swallow demonstrates a thin mucosal fold projecting into the lumen of the upper esophagus. CBC reveals Hb 7.8 g/dL with microcytosis and hypochromia. Serum ferritin is 6 ng/mL. Which malignancy is this patient at significantly increased risk of developing? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1612]
explanation: Plummer-Vinson syndrome presents with the triad of iron deficiency anemia, esophageal webs, and dysphagia. Patients often present with koilonychia and glossitis and carry an increased risk of developing esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1613): Salicylate (aspirin) overdose classically presents with a mixed acid-base disturbance consisting of primary respiratory alkalosis and which second primary disturbance?
option_a: Pure normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
option_b: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_c: Primary metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation
option_d: Primary respiratory acidosis and primary metabolic alkalosis
option_e: Primary respiratory alkalosis and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis
explanation: Salicylate toxicity causes a early direct stimulation of the medullary respiratory center causing primary respiratory alkalosis, followed by uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation leading to organic acid accumulation and primary high anion gap metabolic acidosis. The pH is often near-normal due to opposing primary processes.

question: A 30-year-old male sustains a knife wound to the posterior thorax at the level of T8. Neurological examination reveals right-sided spastic paresis below T8, right-sided loss of tactile discrimination, vibration, and proprioception below T8, and left-sided loss of pain and temperature sensation starting at the T10 dermatome. What anatomical tract decussates in the anterior white commissure of the spinal cord 1-2 segments above entry, explaining the contralateral pain/temp loss? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1614]
explanation: Brown-Séquard syndrome (spinal cord hemisection) injures the ipsilateral corticospinal tract (ipsilateral motor loss), ipsilateral dorsal columns (ipsilateral vibration/proprioception loss), and ipsilateral spinothalamic tract. Because spinothalamic fibers cross in the anterior white commissure 1-2 segments above entry, pain/temp loss is contralateral and begins 1-2 levels below the lesion.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1615): Idiopathy Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by progressive exertional dyspnea, end-inspiratory subpleural crackles, digital clubbing, and which characteristic CT chest finding?
option_d: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (Usual Interstitial Pneumonia pattern)
explanation: Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) presents with restrictive lung disease pattern (decreased FVC and FEV1, increased or normal FEV1/FVC, decreased DLCO), end-inspiratory Velcro crackles, clubbing, and classic HRCT findings of subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.

question: A 42-year-old HIV-positive man with a CD4+ T-cell count of 45/mm³ presents with progressive headache, fever, neck stiffness, and confusion over 2 weeks. Lumbar puncture demonstrates elevated opening pressure (320 mm H2O), lymphocytic pleocytosis, low glucose, and high protein. India ink preparation of CSF demonstrates round budding yeast cells with clear halo-like translucent capsules. Mucicarmine stain shows bright red capsular staining. What is the infectious agent? [Unique Exam Ref FA2023-B4-1616]
explanation: Cryptococcus neoformans is an opportunistic encapsulated yeast found in pigeon droppings. It causes cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients (HIV CD4 <100). Diagnosis is confirmed by CSF India ink (halo around capsule), Mucicarmine stain (red capsule), and Latex agglutination test for capsular polysaccharide antigen.

question: High-Yield Clinical Question (Ref #1617): Which large-vessel vasculitis affects Asian females under 40 years, presenting with weak or absent upper extremity pulses ('pulseless disease') and granulomatous inflammation of the aortic arch?
explanation: Takayasu arteritis ('pulseless disease') is a granulomatous vasculitis of the aortic arch and its major branch vessels, predominantly affecting Asian women <40 years. It presents with fever, night sweats, asymmetric blood pressure/pulses in limbs, ocular disturbances, and elevated ESR.
